text:
sophia: FYI I spotted a surge in config-change telemetry this morning after turning on preview snapshots. The metric 'events.change_applied' doubled for ~40m starting ~09:02. Anybody else seeing this? :thinking:

matt: I remember a similar blip last quarter. That one was caused by the dry-run reconciliation replaying and emitting duplicate events. Was audit-replay on?

sophia: No audit replay. We had preview-snapshot=true and sampling=0.1 for the rollout. Spike aligns with the snapshot window exactly.

eva: Can you share a sanitized example of the event payloads? Quick suspicion: console and orchestrator both emitting "change_applied" for the same change id.

sophia: Minimal payload below (ids redacted):
```
{
  event: "change_applied",
  change_id: "cfg_0xabc123",
  source: "console.preview-snapshot",
  sampling: 0.1,
  delta: { from: 0.2, to: 0.25 }
}
```

zach: That "source" field is the issue. We should normalize to origin and only let the orchestration service emit canonical "change_applied". Console should emit "preview_request" and the orchestrator should emit the canonical event when it actually applies the change.

matt: Short term fix: add a dedupe key to telemetry that uses change_id + origin_type. Longer term: change the event contract so only one service writes "change_applied".

sophia: For dedupe, client-side (console) filter or server-side dedupe in the metrics pipeline? Client-side would avoid extra ingestion cost but is harder to coordinate across SDK versions. Server-side is easier to enforce centrally but adds processing delay. Thoughts?

eva: Server-side. We already have a streaming dedupe step in metrics-ingestor. Add a lightweight 1hr sliding window keyed by (change_id, fingerprint) to drop duplicates and short replays.

zach: Make sure the fingerprint includes commit_sha + action_type so we don't mask legitimate re-applies or rollbacks. Pure change_id dedupe could hide valid repeated operations.

sophia: Can we add commit_sha to console preview payloads? I can update the console SDK to include it. Also proposing a new dashboard metric: slo_burn_by_change that maps change_id to SLO percentiles (latency/error) so we can quickly see impact after deployment.
matt: +1 on slo_burn_by_change. Implementation plan: tag traces during rollout with change_id, then have the metrics job join traces to SLO windows. Might be heavier but very useful when a change correlates with an SLO regression.
eva: UX idea for console: show a small telemetry-health badge during preview snapshots (green/yellow/red). Badge driven by event coverage, dedupe ratio, and time-from-first-event. That helps PMs/ENG know whether telemetry is reliable enough to promote.
sophia: Proposed next steps I can take today:
- Add commit_sha and origin_type to console preview payloads (PR for SDK)
- File a ticket to add server-side dedupe in metrics-ingestor (1hr sliding window, key = change_id + commit_sha + action_type)
- Prototype slo_burn_by_change query in the metrics notebook (join traces -> requests -> rolling SLO)

Who can pair on the dedupe patch?
zach: I can pair tomorrow for 30m to help with sliding-window logic and cardinality constraints.
matt: I'll take the console SDK change to add commit_sha and origin_type.
deploy-bot: Heads-up: metrics-ingestor maintenance scheduled 02:00 UTC tomorrow; consumer groups will restart briefly. :wrench:
sophia: Ok we'll avoid deploying the dedupe patch during that maintenance window. I'll create the ticket and link the planned PRs. Thanks! :thumbsup:
